A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPMF study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Retained, relocated, and newly added material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v4 reports original Gaussian simulations, Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll experiments, SB benchmark evaluations, and colored MNIST and CelebA translation results.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and additionally reports AFHQ translation, initialization-only measurements, and CelebA experiments with epsilon = 10.

M1.justification: The IPMF projection sequence, DSBM/ASBM implementations, and initialization constructions are retained in Sections 3.1, C.4, and E.3. Applying DSBM to AFHQ introduces no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v5 adds AFHQ cat-to-wild translation at 512×512 resolution in Section 4.4. This substantially extends real-image coverage beyond digits and human faces at 32×32 and 64×64 to high-resolution animal domains. Earlier datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: The CelebA comparisons now score initialization-only outputs from IMF, DDPM SDEdit, SD SDEdit, and Identity alongside fitted solvers in Tables 2, 7, and 8. v4 tabulated only fitted solvers. The SB benchmark comparator set, including SF2M-Sink, is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a CelebA Identity condition at epsilon = 10 and an AFHQ protocol with 100,000 pretraining updates followed by 20 DSBM iterations of 25,000 updates each. Existing experimental settings, including the hyperparameter table in v4 Table 6 and v5 Table 9, are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.4 adds a noise-sensitivity comparison for Identity initialization using epsilon = 10 versus the retained epsilon = 1 setting, with Figure 8 and Table 7. Initialization-only scores also enable direct assessment of refinement from the starting coupling. Existing CelebA iteration curves are redistributed, not newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Appendix E.7 retains the same Monte Carlo estimation procedures using 1,000 and 10,000 samples.

E6.justification: v5 adds AFHQ scores, initialization-only metrics, and CelebA epsilon = 10 results. It also swaps the CelebA solver-attributed FID/MSE blocks: Table 2 changes DSBM-IMF FID from 19.32 to 13.65 and ASBM-IMF from 13.65 to 19.32, while the plots retain earlier attribution. Table 8 reverses DSBM's SD/DDPM SDEdit CMMD assignments of 0.46 and 0.34. These are substantial reported-result changes, not established performance improvements; SB benchmark values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 extends bounded-support convergence from discrete-time IPMF to both discrete and continuous time. Appendix D.7 adds a continuous-time argument involving drift regularity, dissipativity, heat-kernel bounds, Doeblin minorization, and weak continuity. The Gaussian analysis and existing discrete-time proof are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction's theoretical contribution removes the discrete-time restriction on bounded-support convergence, matching the expanded Theorem 3.3. This substantially broadens a central convergence guarantee. The claims about unifying IPF/IMF and controlling the quality–similarity tradeoff through initialization remain.

C2.justification: v5 removes the suggestion that SDEdit initialization accelerates convergence and potentially reduces training time. Section 4.4 instead emphasizes how initialization quality and similarity influence corresponding final metrics, and interprets AFHQ as exhibiting a similar tradeoff. Appendix A's general-convergence limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-specific code link in the abstract, beyond the existing implementation references. Appendix E.10 documents AFHQ training budgets, U-Net choice, batch size, EMA, and sampling settings. Existing implementation, preprocessing, and computational-resource disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations to Light Schrödinger Bridge, Light and Optimal Schrödinger Bridge Matching, Choi et al. for AFHQ, and Aronson and Stroock for the new proof. Table 4 summarizes positioning against prior DSBM/ASBM heuristics. The broader research positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most wording and section organization are retained. Changes include localized introduction and experimental-discussion rewrites, discrete/continuous subdivisions in Appendix D.7, an AFHQ subsection, updated affiliations and conference headers, and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially reorganized. Figure 4 is redesigned to display initialization samples beside solver outputs; v4 Figure 6 is split into v5 Figures 5 and 9, moving FID/MSE curves into the main text. CelebA tables gain initialization columns and separate metric displays, while AFHQ, noise-sensitivity, and positioning figures/tables are added.

improvement.justification: The continuous-time analysis, AFHQ evaluation, noise-sensitivity evidence, and project code pointer are useful additions. However, v5 introduces conflicts in central empirical reporting: v4's DSBM-IMF FID of 19.32 agrees with its plotted curve, whereas v5 Table 2 reports 13.65 while Figure 5 retains the curve ending near 19. The accompanying interpretation also retains the earlier attribution. These unresolved conflicts undermine the practical comparisons, making the net quality effect uncertain.
